Safe output for the researcher's script

safe_output.Rd

Three functions for the researcher to use in the script, so the output passes inspect() the first time: counts of persons with small cells suppressed and the rest rounded, summaries of a numeric variable without small or dominated groups, and a table of model coefficients instead of the model object. They apply the same rules as inspect().

Why they exist

Output checkers send output back for the same few reasons again and again. OpenSAFELY reports that about 30 % of rejected requests have counts that are not rounded and 20 % have small counts that are not, or not correctly, suppressed (https://docs.opensafely.org/output-checking/). Suppression is easy to get wrong: a suppressed cell next to a total is the total minus the other cells. inspect() finds these mistakes, but only after the script has run on the real data. These functions do it right in the script, and trial_run() shows the result on the copy.

Which rules apply

Without config the functions use the configuration that trial_run() and real_run() were given: they place it in the script's session as the option mimic.config. The script then follows the rules staff use, without knowing them. Outside those functions the defaults of mimic_config() apply.

Where researchers work on a researcher machine in the secure environment and run their scripts themselves, staff can set the option for every session in the machine's Rprofile.site:

options(mimic.config = mimic::mimic_config(min_count = 5))

With describe_output() the researcher also says what each file shows, so the checker does not have to guess.
